title: Refuse a herding run whose worker claimed success and left its cell uncapped
action: Add a POST-flight cap check to bee herding run, modelled on the preflight_receipt precedent in the same file (run.rs:3952-3973): a DECISION function pure over the filesystem — it reads, it decides, it spawns nothing — so its tests assert the outcome without a process. Place the call in fn run (run.rs:4111-4131), which is the ONE seam both launch paths converge on; record_outcome is NOT that seam (it runs only in execute_new at :2737 and execute_continue at :3497, both pane-only), so D5 is satisfied here and nowhere else. The decision fires ONLY when the worker CLAIMED SUCCESS — RunOutcome::Result(r) with r.status == MailboxStatus::Done, which is exactly the single SUCCESS arm exit_code_for already uses at :3524 — and only when opts.cell_id is Some (D3, D4). When it fires, read that cell's record: if it parses and its status is not capped (no capped_at), the run REFUSES — print to stderr naming the cell id, that the worker reported success without capping, and the verb that settles it, then return ExitCode::FAILURE (D1). REPORT ONLY: never cap the cell, and do not print a ready-to-paste cap line (D2). A missing or unparseable cell file does NOT refuse — return the exit the run would have had (D6). Keep exit_code_for PURE and unchanged: combine its result with the new decision inside fn run, so the existing test at :9621 that calls it directly stays green. Author inline tests in the same file's #[cfg(test)] mod tests covering: claimed-success + uncapped cell refuses; claimed-success + capped cell still succeeds; blocked result with an uncapped cell still exits as today; no cell_id unaffected; missing and unparseable cell files both fall open.
verify: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee --bin bee herding::run

truths: A worker that reports success and leaves its cell claimed makes bee herding run exit non-zero, naming the cell
A worker that reports success on a properly capped cell still exits zero
A blocked, timed-out or failed worker is completely unaffected
No cell is ever capped by this check

checks.evidence: postflight_cap_check returns PostflightCapAction::Refuse { cell_id } when the cell parses and is not capped, and fn run turns that into a non-zero exit with one eprintln! naming the cell. Test postflight_cap_check_refuses_claimed_success_with_uncapped_cell pins it.

Searched the added lines for any write path: the only std::fs::write calls are inside the tests, seeding fixtures including corrupt-cell.json. The decision function reads and returns an enum; it writes nothing and prints no ready-to-paste cap line.

The match arm is `RunOutcome::Result(r) if r.status == MailboxStatus::Done => {}` with `_ => return Proceed`, which is exactly the single SUCCESS arm exit_code_for uses at run.rs:3524. Tests postflight_cap_check_proceeds_on_blocked_result_with_uncapped_cell and _proceeds_on_non_done_outcomes pin both halves.

`let Some(cell_id) = cell_id else { return Proceed }` is the first statement. Test postflight_cap_check_proceeds_when_no_cell_id pins it, so gather, advisor, hat and reviewer dispatches are untouched.

The call sits in fn run (run.rs:4111-4131), after `let result = if opts.no_pane { execute_no_pane } else { execute }`, so both launch paths reach it. record_outcome was NOT used, correctly: it runs only in execute_new (:2737) and execute_continue (:3497), both pane-only.

`let Ok(raw) = std::fs::read_to_string(&cell_path) else { return Proceed }`, and an unparseable body returns Proceed too. Tests postflight_cap_check_falls_open_on_missing_cell_file and _on_unparseable_cell_file pin both.

fn exit_code_for is still at run.rs:3521 with an unchanged signature over &RunOutcome, so the pre-existing test at :9621 that calls it directly is unaffected. That purity is what let the lane de-escalate to small.

Zero Command::new or spawn( additions in the diff. The decision is pure over the filesystem, following the preflight_receipt precedent at run.rs:3952-3973, whose own comment records 12 leaked agent sessions in one day as the reason that rule exists.
